Nina: anyone seen flaky failures around api key rotation with the py async client? tests pass locally but CI flakes when running in parallel
Theo: saw one yesterday but assumed my change. can you share a tiny repro?
Nina: minimal gist here: https://gist.github.com/nina/rotate-mini (basically two AsyncClient instances + os.environ flip while tasks run)
Nina: repro snippet: ```python
import os, asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def call(c):
    await c.generate('x')

async def main():
    os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'] = 'A'
    c1 = AsyncClient()
    task1 = asyncio.create_task(call(c1))
    os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'] = 'B'
    c2 = AsyncClient()
    await asyncio.gather(task1, call(c2))

asyncio.run(main())
```
Priya: interesting. is the client reading env only at init? we might be caching Authorization value on the connection pool which would explain it.
Alex: yeah the pool attaches headers to each connection on first use. if env rotates mid-run existing connections keep old header.
Nina: workaround that fixed my CI: explicitly pass api_key when constructing client or call client.aclose() before rotating env. but both are awkward for k8s secret sync patterns.
Theo: for short term let's add a test that spawns multiple tasks and toggles env; CI should catch it. longer term we should provide a reload() or make header retrieval per-request when provider is dynamic.
Priya: typing improvement idea: instead of Optional[Union[str, Callable[[], str]]], add a Protocol ApiKeyProvider so mypy users can pass typed factories. also document precedence order: explicit param > env var > credential file.
Alex: good call. also add a docs blurb: avoid creating clients at import time if you expect rotating credentials. put in startup hook.
ops-bot: created ticket #3478 in py-sdk with repro and labels: sdk/py bug auth-rotation at 1812345689
Nina: thanks! leaving logs and stack trace in the ticket. will follow up with a small PR for the tests.
Theo: I can review the PR. Priya can you draft the typing change?
Priya: on it, will post proposal in the issue.
Nina: copying workaround into our internal onboarding guide so new engineers don't hit the same trap.
